facts.fact: 图书室又冷又静；她吃着当天的草莓马卡龙，却听不见他办公室方向一点声响——没有他唤 Fletcher 的吼声，也没有股价单机器的转动声。
facts.anchor: Once again, I couldn’t hear a thing coming from the direction of his office.

facts.fact: 他已经躲了她将近一周，像躲一个得了伤寒的人；Fletcher 只说主人没病、让她不必担心。
facts.anchor: for him to avoid me as if I had typhoid

facts.fact: 她想听 Zane 讲自己的成长：磨坊爆炸之后他赤手空起家做出一份产业；她说他是"a fascinating man"。
facts.anchor: how he’d recovered after the mill explosion to build an empire with his bare hands
And yes, I could admit it. I missed him.

facts.fact: 密道尽头是一间藏满书的阳台，正对着她在图书室书桌的位置——站在那儿的人可以在阴影里无声地看着她。
facts.anchor: There was . . . a direct view of where I sat at the desk

facts.fact: 她向 Fletcher 喊出自己的诉求：只想要一处能独自读书、不被窥探、也不受男人支配的空间。
facts.anchor: All I wanted was a quiet space to be alone with books, to be free of prying eyes and controlling men.

facts.fact: Zane 本人出现在华盛顿广场公园的长椅上，帽子压低遮住脸；他就坐在她身边。
facts.anchor: My head snapped up. Zane was on the bench, directly beside me, his hat pulled low to obscure his face.

facts.fact: 他西行五天、返程四天找到 Orson，说服他在离婚文件上签字；文件送回她手上时，她说自己自由了。
facts.anchor: It took five days there, four days back.
